उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of magnetic field dependence on solenoid radius
Using Ampere's circuital law, the magnetic field inside an ideal, tightly wound, infinitely long solenoid carrying current \(I\) with \(n\) turns per unit length is given by \(B = \mu_0 n I\). This field is completely uniform throughout the internal volume of the solenoid and depends solely on the permeability of free space \(\mu_0\), the linear turn density \(n\), and the current \(I\). It is strictly independent of the radius or cross-sectional shape of the solenoid. Therefore, asserting that the internal magnetic field depends directly on the radius is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of magnetic field at the solenoid ends
For a long solenoid of finite length where the midpoint field is \(B_{\text{center}} = \mu_0 n I\), the magnetic field at the extreme ends along the axis subtends only half the solid angle of the midpoint. Evaluating the field using the Biot-Savart integration gives \(B_{\text{end}} = \frac{1}{2}\mu_0 n I = \frac{1}{2}B_{\text{center}}\). Thus, the field at the ends is half of the center value, not twice. Therefore, the assertion that the end field is twice the midpoint field is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and conclusion
The internal field is independent of the solenoid cross-sectional radius, and the axial field at the ends is half (not twice) the center field. Both propositions are incorrect.

Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: परिनालिका की त्रिज्या पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
ऐम्पियर के परिपथीय नियम के अनुप्रयोग से, प्रति एकांक लंबाई \(n\) फेरों वाली तथा \(I\) धारा प्रवाहित करने वाली किसी आदर्श अनंत लंबी परिनालिका के भीतर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(B = \mu_0 n I\) होता है। यह क्षेत्र परिनालिका के आंतरिक आयतन में सर्वत्र एकसमान होता है और केवल \(\mu_0\), फेरों के रेखीय घनत्व \(n\) तथा धारा \(I\) पर निर्भर करता है। यह परिनालिका की त्रिज्या या अनुप्रस्थ काट की आकृति पर बिल्कुल निर्भर नहीं करता। अतः यह कहना कि आंतरिक चुंबकीय क्षेत्र त्रिज्या पर प्रत्यक्ष निर्भर करता है, गलत है।

चरण 2: परिनालिका के सिरों पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र का मूल्यांकन
परिमित लंबाई की लंबी परिनालिका के लिए जिसके केंद्र पर क्षेत्र \(B_{\text{center}} = \mu_0 n I\) होता है, अक्ष के अनुदिश अंतिम सिरों पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र केंद्र के ठोस कोण का आधा अंतरित करता है। बायो-सावर्ट नियम के समाकलन द्वारा सिरों पर क्षेत्र \(B_{\text{end}} = \frac{1}{2}\mu_0 n I = \frac{1}{2}B_{\text{center}}\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः सिरों पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र केंद्र के मान का आधा होता है न कि दोगुना। इसलिए सिरों पर दोगुना क्षेत्र बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
आंतरिक क्षेत्र परिनालिका की अनुप्रस्थ काट की त्रिज्या से स्वतंत्र होता है, तथा सिरों पर अक्षीय क्षेत्र केंद्र के मान का आधा (दोगुना नहीं) होता है। अतः दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q06 - Conversion and circuit connection of an ammeter

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: To measure the electric current flowing through a circuit branch, an ammeter must be connected in parallel with that branch.

Statement II: A moving coil galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting a very small resistance in parallel with its coil.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी परिपथ शाखा में प्रवाहित विद्युत धारा मापने के लिए अमीटर को उस शाखा के समांतर क्रम में जोड़ा जाना चाहिए।

कथन II: किसी चल कुंडली धारामापी को उसकी कुंडली के समांतर क्रम में एक अल्प प्रतिरोध जोड़कर अमीटर में रूपांतरित किया जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of ammeter connection in an electrical circuit
An ammeter is designed to measure the rate of charge flow through a given circuit branch. In order for the full current of the branch to pass through the instrument without altering the branch current significantly, the ammeter must possess very low resistance and must be connected in series with the branch. Connecting an ammeter in parallel across a branch would create a low-resistance short circuit, drawing excessive current and failing to measure the original branch current. Hence, asserting that an ammeter is connected in parallel is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of galvanometer conversion into an ammeter
A moving coil galvanometer has a coil of resistance \(G\) that achieves full-scale deflection with a small current \(I_g\). To allow it to measure a much larger total current \(I\), a low resistance \(r_s\) (called a shunt) is connected in parallel with the galvanometer coil. The major portion of current \((I - I_g)\) bypasses the coil through the shunt, while the overall equivalent resistance becomes \(R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{G r_s}{G + r_s} \approx r_s \ll G\), thereby transforming the galvanometer into an effective ammeter. Thus, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Synthesis and conclusion
An ammeter must be connected in series with the branch to measure current, and a galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting a small shunt resistance in parallel. Thus, the first proposition is incorrect while the second proposition is correct.

Final Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: विद्युत परिपथ में अमीटर के संयोजन का मूल्यांकन
अमीटर को किसी परिपथ शाखा में आवेश प्रवाह की दर (धारा) मापने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। शाखा की संपूर्ण धारा उपकरण से होकर प्रवाहित हो सके और शाखा के मूल प्रतिरोध में न्यूनतम परिवर्तन हो, इसके लिए अमीटर का प्रतिरोध अत्यंत कम होना चाहिए तथा इसे शाखा के श्रेणीक्रम में जोड़ा जाना अनिवार्य है। अमीटर को समांतर क्रम में जोड़ने पर यह एक लघुपथ (शॉर्ट सर्किट) बना देगा, जिससे अत्यधिक धारा बहेगी और वास्तविक धारा का मापन नहीं हो सकेगा। अतः अमीटर को समांतर क्रम में जोड़ने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: धारामापी का अमीटर में रूपांतरण का मूल्यांकन
चल कुंडली धारामापी की कुंडली का प्रतिरोध \(G\) होता है और यह अल्प धारा \(I_g\) पर पूर्ण पैमाना विक्षेप देता है। इसे एक वृहत धारा \(I\) मापने योग्य बनाने के लिए धारामापी कुंडली के समांतर क्रम में एक अल्प प्रतिरोध \(r_s\) (शंट) जोड़ा जाता है। धारा का अधिकांश भाग \((I - I_g)\) शंट से होकर निकल जाता है तथा संयुक्त तुल्य प्रतिरोध \(R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{G r_s}{G + r_s} \approx r_s \ll G\) अत्यंत कम हो जाता है। यह युक्ति को एक प्रभावी अमीटर बना देता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
धारा मापने के लिए अमीटर को श्रेणीक्रम में जोड़ा जाना चाहिए, तथा धारामापी को अमीटर में बदलने के लिए समांतर क्रम में अल्प शंट प्रतिरोध जोड़ा जाता है। अतः पहला कथन गलत है जबकि दूसरा कथन सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q07 - Galvanometer current and voltage sensitivity with turns

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Doubling the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer doubles its current sensitivity.

Statement II: Doubling the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer also doubles its voltage sensitivity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी चल कुंडली धारामापी की कुंडली में फेरों की संख्या दोगुनी करने पर इसकी धारा सुग्राहिता दोगुनी हो जाती है।

कथन II: किसी चल कुंडली धारामापी की कुंडली में फेरों की संख्या दोगुनी करने पर इसकी वोल्टता सुग्राहिता भी दोगुनी हो जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of current sensitivity
The equilibrium deflection \(\theta\) of a moving coil galvanometer is governed by the restoring torque balancing the magnetic deflecting torque: \(k\theta = N I A B\), where \(N\) is the number of turns, \(I\) is the current, \(A\) is coil area, \(B\) is magnetic field, and \(k\) is the torsional restoring constant per unit twist. Current sensitivity is defined as deflection per unit current: \(S_i = \frac{\theta}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\). Since \(S_i \propto N\), doubling the number of turns from \(N\) to \(2N\) while holding \(A\), \(B\), and \(k\) constant doubles the current sensitivity: \(S_i' = 2 S_i\). Thus, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of voltage sensitivity
Voltage sensitivity is defined as deflection per unit potential difference: \(S_v = \frac{\theta}{V} = \frac{\theta}{I R} = \frac{S_i}{R} = \frac{N A B}{k R}\), where \(R\) is the electrical resistance of the galvanometer coil. When the number of turns is doubled from \(N\) to \(2N\) using wire of the same cross-sectional area, the total length of the wire doubles, which in turn doubles the coil resistance from \(R\) to \(2R\). Consequently, the new voltage sensitivity is \(S_v' = \frac{(2N) A B}{k (2R)} = \frac{N A B}{k R} = S_v\). Therefore, doubling the number of turns leaves the voltage sensitivity unchanged. Hence, asserting that voltage sensitivity doubles is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and conclusion
Doubling the number of turns doubles current sensitivity, but because coil resistance simultaneously doubles, voltage sensitivity remains unchanged. Thus, the first proposition is correct while the second proposition is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: धारा सुग्राहिता का विश्लेषण
चल कुंडली धारामापी का साम्यावस्था विक्षेप \(\theta\) चुंबकीय विक्षेपक आघूर्ण और प्रत्यानयन आघूर्ण के संतुलन द्वारा निर्धारित होता है: \(k\theta = N I A B\), जहाँ \(N\) फेरों की संख्या, \(I\) धारा, \(A\) कुंडली का क्षेत्रफल, \(B\) चुंबकीय क्षेत्र तथा \(k\) मरोड़ी नियतांक है। धारा सुग्राहिता को प्रति एकांक धारा विक्षेप के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है: \(S_i = \frac{\theta}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\)। चूँकि \(S_i \propto N\), अतः अन्य कारकों को नियत रखते हुए फेरों की संख्या \(N\) से \(2N\) करने पर धारा सुग्राहिता दोगुनी (\(S_i' = 2 S_i\)) हो जाती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: वोल्टता सुग्राहिता का विश्लेषण
वोल्टता सुग्राहिता प्रति एकांक विभवांतर विक्षेप के रूप में परिभाषित होती है: \(S_v = \frac{\theta}{V} = \frac{S_i}{R} = \frac{N A B}{k R}\), जहाँ \(R\) कुंडली का प्रतिरोध है। समान अनुप्रस्थ काट वाले तार से फेरों की संख्या \(N\) से \(2N\) करने पर तार की कुल लंबाई दोगुनी हो जाती है, जिससे कुंडली का प्रतिरोध भी \(R\) से बढ़कर \(2R\) हो जाता है। अतः नई वोल्टता सुग्राहिता \(S_v' = \frac{(2N) A B}{k (2R)} = \frac{N A B}{k R} = S_v\) अपरिवर्तित रहती है। इसलिए वोल्टता सुग्राहिता के दोगुने होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
फेरों की संख्या दोगुनी करने पर धारा सुग्राहिता दोगुनी हो जाती है, परंतु कुंडली का प्रतिरोध भी दोगुना होने के कारण वोल्टता सुग्राहिता अपरिवर्तित रहती है। अतः पहला कथन सही है जबकि दूसरा कथन गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q08 - Applicability and theoretical validity of Ampere law

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ampere's circuital law can be practically used to evaluate the magnetic field at any arbitrary point off the axis of a circular current-carrying loop.

Statement II: Ampere's circuital law holds theoretically for any arbitrary closed loop enclosing steady currents, regardless of its geometric symmetry.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी वृत्ताकार धारावाही लूप के अक्ष से परे किसी भी यादृच्छिक बिंदु पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र का सरलता से मान निकालने के लिए ऐम्पियर का परिपथीय नियम व्यावहारिक रूप से प्रयुक्त किया जा सकता है।

कथन II: ऐम्पियर का परिपथीय नियम लूप की ज्यामितीय सममिति पर ध्यान दिए बिना, स्थिर धाराओं को घेरने वाले किसी भी यादृच्छिक बंद लूप के लिए सैद्धांतिक रूप से मान्य है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of practical applicability of Ampere's circuital law
Ampere's circuital law states that \(\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{\text{enclosed}}\). To practically extract \(|\vec{B}|\) from within the line integral, the chosen Amperian path must possess high spatial symmetry such that \(\vec{B}\) has a constant magnitude tangential to the path (or is perpendicular to the path, or vanishes). For a circular current loop, the magnetic field at arbitrary off-axis points lacks cylindrical or axial symmetry; no Amperian loop can be chosen along which \(|\vec{B}|\) is constant and tangential. Hence, Ampere's circuital law cannot be practically used to calculate the magnetic field at arbitrary off-axis points (which requires Biot-Savart integration). Therefore, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of general theoretical validity of Ampere's circuital law
Ampere's circuital law is one of the foundational equations of electromagnetism for magnetostatics. It is mathematically and physically exact for any closed path of arbitrary shape enclosing steady currents, identical to how Gauss's law for electrostatics holds for any closed surface regardless of whether symmetry allows calculating the field. The limitation in extracting \(\vec{B}\) is purely mathematical/practical, not a failure of the law itself. Thus, Ampere's circuital law is universally valid in theory for all closed loops enclosing steady currents, making this proposition correct.

Step 3: Synthesis and conclusion
Ampere's circuital law holds theoretically for every closed path enclosing steady currents, but high geometric symmetry is essential to use it practically to compute the magnetic field. Thus, the first proposition is incorrect while the second proposition is correct.

Final Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: ऐम्पियर के परिपथीय नियम की व्यावहारिक प्रयोज्यता का विश्लेषण
ऐम्पियर का परिपथीय नियम व्यक्त करता है कि \(\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{\text{enclosed}}\)। रेखा समाकल से \(|\vec{B}|\) का व्यावहारिक मान ज्ञात करने के लिए, चुने गए ऐम्पियरीय लूप में उच्च स्थानिक सममिति होनी चाहिए ताकि \(\vec{B}\) का परिमाण लूप के स्पर्शरेखीय नियत रहे (अथवा लूप के लंबवत हो या शून्य हो)। किसी वृत्ताकार धारा लूप के अक्ष से परे बिंदुओं पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में बेलनाकार सममिति नहीं होती; अतः ऐसा कोई ऐम्पियरीय लूप नहीं चुना जा सकता जिसके अनुदिश \(|\vec{B}|\) नियत व स्पर्शरेखीय हो। इसलिए ऐसे बिंदुओं पर क्षेत्र निकालने हेतु इस नियम का व्यावहारिक उपयोग नहीं किया जा सकता (इसके लिए बायो-सावर्ट नियम आवश्यक है)। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: ऐम्पियर के परिपथीय नियम की सैद्धांतिक मान्यता का विश्लेषण
स्थिर चुंबकत्व के लिए ऐम्पियर का परिपथीय नियम विद्युत-चुंबकत्व का एक मूलभूत नियम है। यह स्थिर धाराओं को घेरने वाले किसी भी यादृच्छिक आकृति के बंद पथ के लिए सैद्धांतिक एवं भौतिक रूप से पूर्णतः सत्य है, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे गाउस का नियम किसी भी बंद पृष्ठ के लिए सत्य होता है भले ही सममिति के अभाव में क्षेत्र की गणना संभव न हो। \(\vec{B}\) को समाकल से बाहर न निकाल पाना केवल गणितीय सीमा है, नियम की विफलता नहीं। अतः ऐम्पियर का नियम सैद्धांतिक रूप से सदैव मान्य है, इसलिए यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
ऐम्पियर का परिपथीय नियम स्थिर धाराओं को घेरने वाले प्रत्येक बंद पथ के लिए सैद्धांतिक रूप से सत्य है, परंतु चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की गणना हेतु व्यावहारिक उपयोग के लिए उच्च सममिति अनिवार्य है। अतः पहला कथन गलत है जबकि दूसरा कथन सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q01 - Lorentz force and cyclotron frequency independence

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The magnetic Lorentz force acting on a moving charged particle is always perpendicular to both its instantaneous velocity and the external magnetic field.

Statement II: A charged particle entering a uniform magnetic field with its velocity parallel to the field lines describes a circular trajectory.

Statement III: The cyclotron frequency of a charged particle executing circular motion in a uniform magnetic field is independent of its speed and kinetic energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी गतिमान आवेशित कण पर कार्य करने वाला चुंबकीय लॉरेंट्ज़ बल सदैव उसके तात्क्षणिक वेग तथा बाह्य चुंबकीय क्षेत्र दोनों के लंबवत होता है।

कथन II: चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं के समांतर वेग से एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में प्रवेश करने वाला कोई आवेशित कण वृत्ताकार प्रक्षेप-पथ का अनुसरण करता है।

कथन III: एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में वृत्तीय गति करते हुए किसी आवेशित कण की साइक्लोट्रॉन आवृत्ति उसकी चाल तथा गतिज ऊर्जा पर निर्भर नहीं करती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of magnetic Lorentz force directionality
The magnetic Lorentz force on a charged particle of charge \(q\) moving with velocity \(\vec{v}\) in a magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) is given by the cross product \(\vec{F}_m = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})\). By definition of the vector cross product, \(\vec{F}_m\) is strictly perpendicular to the plane containing \(\vec{v}\) and \(\vec{B}\). Thus, the force is always perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field, making this proposition correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of particle trajectory when velocity is parallel to the magnetic field
When a charged particle moves parallel to the magnetic field lines, the angle between \(\vec{v}\) and \(\vec{B}\) is \(\theta = 0^{\circ}\). The magnitude of the magnetic force is \(F_m = q v B \sin(0^{\circ}) = 0\). Since the net magnetic force is zero, the particle experiences no acceleration and continues to move in a straight line with constant velocity, not in a circular path. Hence, the proposition claiming a circular trajectory is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of cyclotron frequency dependence on speed and energy
When a charged particle moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, the centripetal force is provided by the magnetic force: \(\frac{m v^2}{r} = q v B\), yielding the radius \(r = \frac{m v}{q B}\). The frequency of revolution (cyclotron frequency) is \(\nu = \frac{v}{2\pi r} = \frac{q B}{2\pi m}\). This frequency depends exclusively on the charge \(q\), mass \(m\), and magnetic field \(B\), and is completely independent of the particle's speed \(v\) and kinetic energy. Thus, this proposition is correct.

Step 4: Synthesis and conclusion
The propositions regarding Lorentz force direction and cyclotron frequency independence are correct, while the proposition regarding motion parallel to the field is incorrect. Therefore, Statement I and Statement III only are correct.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement III only are correct.

चरण 1: चुंबकीय लॉरेंट्ज़ बल की दिशा का मूल्यांकन
चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(\vec{B}\) में \(\vec{v}\) वेग से गतिमान आवेश \(q\) वाले कण पर लगने वाला चुंबकीय लॉरेंट्ज़ बल सदिश गुणनफल \(\vec{F}_m = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})\) द्वारा दिया जाता है। सदिश गुणनफल की परिभाषा के अनुसार, \(\vec{F}_m\) सदैव \(\vec{v}\) और \(\vec{B}\) दोनों के लंबवत होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: चुंबकीय क्षेत्र के समांतर वेग होने पर प्रक्षेप-पथ का मूल्यांकन
जब कोई आवेशित कण चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं के समांतर गति करता है, तो \(\vec{v}\) और \(\vec{B}\) के बीच का कोण \(\theta = 0^{\circ}\) होता है। चुंबकीय बल का परिमाण \(F_m = q v B \sin(0^{\circ}) = 0\) हो जाता है। बल शून्य होने के कारण कण बिना किसी विक्षेप के एक सीधी रेखा में गति करता है, वृत्ताकार पथ पर नहीं। अतः वृत्ताकार प्रक्षेप-पथ का दावा करने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: चाल तथा ऊर्जा पर साइक्लोट्रॉन आवृत्ति की निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र के लंबवत गति करते कण के लिए चुंबकीय बल अभिककेंद्रीय बल प्रदान करता है: \(\frac{m v^2}{r} = q v B\), जिससे \(r = \frac{m v}{q B}\) प्राप्त होता है। परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति (साइक्लोट्रॉन आवृत्ति) \(\nu = \frac{v}{2\pi r} = \frac{q B}{2\pi m}\) होती है। यह आवृत्ति केवल आवेश \(q\), द्रव्यमान \(m\) तथा चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(B\) पर निर्भर करती है और कण की चाल \(v\) अथवा गतिज ऊर्जा से स्वतंत्र होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
लॉरेंट्ज़ बल की दिशा तथा साइक्लोट्रॉन आवृत्ति की चाल से स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि समांतर गति से संबंधित कथन गलत है। अतः केवल कथन I और कथन III सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I and Statement II only are correct.
Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q02 - Biot Savart law and circular loop field

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The Biot-Savart law states that the magnitude of the magnetic field produced by an elemental current segment is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the segment.

Statement II: The magnitude of the magnetic field produced at the center of a circular loop of radius \(R\) carrying steady current \(I\) is \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\).

Statement III: Along the axis of a circular current-carrying loop, the magnetic field component perpendicular to the axis does not vanish when integrated over the entire circumference.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बायो-सावर्ट नियम के अनुसार किसी अल्पांश धारा खंड द्वारा उत्पन्न चुंबकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण उस खंड से प्रेक्षण बिंदु की दूरी के वर्ग के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है।

कथन II: स्थिर धारा \(I\) प्रवाहित करने वाले \(R\) त्रिज्या के वृत्ताकार लूप के केंद्र पर उत्पन्न चुंबकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\) होता है।

कथन III: किसी वृत्ताकार धारावाही लूप के अक्ष के अनुदिश, पूरी परिधि पर समाकलन करने पर अक्ष के लंबवत चुंबकीय क्षेत्र घटक का मान शून्य नहीं होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Biot-Savart distance dependence
According to the Biot-Savart law, the infinitesimal magnetic field \(d\vec{B}\) due to a current element \(I\,d\vec{l}\) at a displacement vector \(\vec{r}\) is given by \(d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I(d\vec{l} \times \hat{r})}{r^2}\). The magnitude is \(|d\vec{B}| = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I\,dl\sin\theta}{r^2}\), which explicitly obeys an inverse-square dependence on distance \(r\). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the magnetic field at the center of a circular loop
For a circular loop of radius \(R\) carrying current \(I\), every current element \(d\vec{l}\) is perpendicular to the position vector from the element to the center (\(\theta = 90^{\circ}\)), and all elements are equidistant at \(r = R\). Integrating over the loop circumference gives \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2} \oint dl = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2} (2\pi R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of off-axis perpendicular field components
At any point on the axis of a circular current loop, the magnetic field contribution \(d\vec{B}\) from a current element can be resolved into a component along the axis (\(dB_x = dB\cos\theta\)) and a component perpendicular to the axis (\(dB_\perp = dB\sin\theta\)). Due to circular symmetry, for every infinitesimal element \(d\vec{l}\), there exists a diametrically opposite element whose perpendicular component \(dB_\perp\) is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Consequently, the perpendicular components completely cancel out upon summation over the closed loop, leaving only the axial component. Therefore, asserting that the perpendicular component does not vanish is incorrect.

Step 4: Synthesis and conclusion
The propositions regarding the inverse-square law and the center field formula are correct, while the proposition regarding non-vanishing perpendicular components is incorrect. Therefore, Statement I and Statement II only are correct.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement II only are correct.

चरण 1: बायो-सावर्ट नियम की दूरी पर निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
बायो-सावर्ट नियम के अनुसार, विस्थापन सदिश \(\vec{r}\) पर धारा अल्पांश \(I\,d\vec{l}\) के कारण चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I(d\vec{l} \times \hat{r})}{r^2}\) होता है। इसका परिमाण \(|d\vec{B}| = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I\,dl\sin\theta}{r^2}\) स्पष्ट रूप से दूरी \(r\) के व्युत्क्रम वर्ग नियम का पालन करता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: वृत्ताकार लूप के केंद्र पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र का मूल्यांकन
त्रिज्या \(R\) तथा धारा \(I\) वाले वृत्ताकार लूप के लिए, प्रत्येक अल्पांश \(d\vec{l}\) केंद्र की ओर जाने वाले सदिश के लंबवत (\(\theta = 90^{\circ}\)) होता है तथा सभी अल्पांश \(R\) दूरी पर स्थित होते हैं। संपूर्ण परिधि पर समाकलन करने पर \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2} (2\pi R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अक्ष के लंबवत चुंबकीय क्षेत्र घटकों का मूल्यांकन
वृत्ताकार धारा लूप के अक्ष पर स्थित बिंदु पर किसी अल्पांश के क्षेत्र \(d\vec{B}\) को अक्षीय घटक तथा अक्ष के लंबवत घटक में वियोजित किया जा सकता है। वृत्तीय सममिति के कारण, प्रत्येक अल्पांश के लिए परिधि पर एक व्यासतः विपरीत अल्पांश उपस्थित होता है जिसका लंबवत घटक परिमाण में समान और दिशा में विपरीत होता है। अतः पूरे लूप पर समाकलन करने पर ये घटक एक-दूसरे को पूर्णतः निरस्त कर देते हैं और केवल अक्षीय घटक शेष रहता है। अतः लंबवत घटक के शून्य न होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
व्युत्क्रम वर्ग नियम और केंद्र पर क्षेत्र के सूत्र से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि लंबवत घटक के निरस्त न होने का कथन गलत है। अतः केवल कथन I और कथन II सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन II सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I and Statement II only are correct.
Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q03 - Ampere definition and torque on current loop

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Two long, straight parallel conductors carrying electric currents in the same direction exert repulsive magnetic forces on each other.

Statement II: One ampere is the steady current which, when maintained in two long, parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed one metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of \(2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ N/m}\) on each conductor.

Statement III: A planar current loop placed in a uniform magnetic field experiences a net magnetic torque given by \(\vec{\tau} = \vec{m} \times \vec{B}\), but experiences zero net magnetic translational force.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक ही दिशा में विद्युत धारा प्रवाहित करने वाले दो लंबे, सीधे समांतर चालक एक-दूसरे पर प्रतिकर्षी चुंबकीय बल लगाते हैं।

कथन II: एक ऐम्पियर वह स्थिर धारा है जो निर्वात में एक मीटर की दूरी पर स्थित नगण्य अनुप्रस्थ काट वाले दो लंबे समांतर चालकों में प्रवाहित होने पर प्रत्येक चालक पर \(2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ N/m}\) का बल उत्पन्न करती है।

कथन III: एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में स्थित कोई समतलीय धारा लूप \(\vec{\tau} = \vec{m} \times \vec{B}\) का परिणामी चुंबकीय बल-आघूर्ण अनुभव करता है, परंतु उस पर परिणामी चुंबकीय स्थानांतरीय बल शून्य होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the magnetic force between parallel conductors
For two parallel straight wires separated by distance \(d\) carrying currents \(I_1\) and \(I_2\) in the same direction, applying the right-hand rule and the Lorentz force equation \(\vec{F} = I(\vec{L} \times \vec{B})\) reveals that the magnetic force on each wire is directed toward the other wire. Hence, parallel currents flowing in the same direction attract each other, whereas antiparallel currents repel. Thus, the proposition asserting repulsion between parallel currents in the same direction is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the SI definition of the ampere
The magnetic force per unit length between two parallel conductors separated by distance \(d\) in vacuum is \(f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}\). When \(I_1 = I_2 = 1\text{ A}\) and \(d = 1\text{ m}\), with \(\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}\), the force per unit length is \(f = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 1 \times 1}{1} = 2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ N/m}\). This represents the official international definition of the base SI unit, the ampere. Therefore, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of torque and net force on a planar loop in a uniform field
In a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\), the net magnetic force on any closed current loop is \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = I \oint d\vec{l} \times \vec{B} = I \left(\oint d\vec{l}\right) \times \vec{B}\). Since the vector displacement around any closed loop is identically zero (\(\oint d\vec{l} = \vec{0}\)), the net translational force is strictly zero. However, the equal and opposite forces acting on separated segments of the loop form a couple, producing a net torque \(\vec{\tau} = \vec{m} \times \vec{B}\), where \(\vec{m} = I\vec{A}\) is the magnetic dipole moment. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 4: Synthesis and conclusion
The proposition asserting repulsion between parallel currents is incorrect, whereas the SI definition of the ampere and the torque expression for a planar loop in a uniform field are correct. Therefore, Statement II and Statement III only are correct.

Final Answer: Statement II and Statement III only are correct.

चरण 1: समांतर चालकों के बीच चुंबकीय बल का मूल्यांकन
दूरी \(d\) पर स्थित दो समांतर सीधे तारों में समान दिशा में धारा प्रवाहित होने पर, दक्षिण-हस्त नियम तथा लॉरेंट्ज़ बल समीकरण \(\vec{F} = I(\vec{L} \times \vec{B})\) के अनुप्रयोग से स्पष्ट होता है कि प्रत्येक तार पर बल दूसरे तार की ओर निर्देशित होता है। अतः समान दिशा की धाराएँ एक-दूसरे को आकर्षित करती हैं (विपरीत दिशा की धाराएँ प्रतिकर्षित करती हैं)। इसलिए समान दिशा की धाराओं में प्रतिकर्षण बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: ऐम्पियर की SI परिभाषा का मूल्यांकन
निर्वात में दूरी \(d\) पर स्थित दो समांतर चालकों के बीच प्रति एकांक लंबाई चुंबकीय बल \(f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}\) होता है। यदि \(I_1 = I_2 = 1\text{ A}\) तथा \(d = 1\text{ m}\) हो, तो \(f = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1 \times 1}{2\pi \times 1} = 2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ N/m}\) प्राप्त होता है। यह ऐम्पियर की प्रामाणिक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय परिभाषा है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: एकसमान क्षेत्र में समतलीय लूप पर बल तथा बल-आघूर्ण का मूल्यांकन
एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(\vec{B}\) में किसी बंद लूप पर कुल बल \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = I \left(\oint d\vec{l}\right) \times \vec{B}\) होता है। किसी भी बंद लूप के लिए \(\oint d\vec{l} = \vec{0}\) होने के कारण परिणामी स्थानांतरीय बल सदैव शून्य होता है। किंतु लूप की विपरीत भुजाओं पर लगने वाले समान तथा विपरीत बल एक बलयुग्म बनाते हैं, जिससे परिणामी बल-आघूर्ण \(\vec{\tau} = \vec{m} \times \vec{B}\) उत्पन्न होता है (जहाँ \(\vec{m} = I\vec{A}\))। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
समान दिशा की धाराओं के प्रतिकर्षण का कथन गलत है, जबकि ऐम्पियर की परिभाषा तथा समतलीय लूप पर बल-आघूर्ण से संबंधित कथन सही हैं। अतः केवल कथन II और कथन III सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल कथन II और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct.
Statement I and Statement III only are correct.
Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MCQ_Q04 - Galvanometer principles and voltmeter ammeter conversion characteristics

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In a moving coil galvanometer, a soft iron core placed inside the coil increases the magnetic field strength and makes the magnetic field radial.

Statement II: Doubling the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer doubles its current sensitivity while keeping its voltage sensitivity unchanged.

Statement III: A moving coil galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting a resistance of large value in series with the galvanometer coil.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी चल कुंडली धारामापी में, कुंडली के भीतर रखा गया नर्म लोहे का क्रोड चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की तीव्रता को बढ़ाता है तथा चुंबकीय क्षेत्र को त्रिज्य बनाता है।

कथन II: किसी चल कुंडली धारामापी की कुंडली में फेरों की संख्या दोगुनी करने पर इसकी धारा सुग्राहिता दोगुनी हो जाती है जबकि इसकी वोल्टता सुग्राहिता अपरिवर्तित रहती है।

कथन III: किसी चल कुंडली धारामापी को उसकी कुंडली के श्रेणीक्रम में एक उच्च मान का प्रतिरोध जोड़कर वोल्टमीटर में रूपांतरित किया जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of soft iron core functionality in a galvanometer
A moving coil galvanometer utilizes concave magnetic pole pieces together with a cylindrical soft iron core placed concentrically within the coil. Soft iron has very high magnetic permeability, which concentrates magnetic flux lines to significantly increase field strength. Furthermore, the cylindrical geometry ensures that magnetic field lines enter and leave normally, making the field radial in the air gap. Consequently, the plane of the coil remains parallel to the magnetic field lines in all angular positions (\(\sin\theta = 1\)), maintaining a constant deflecting torque \(\tau = N I A B\). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of current sensitivity versus voltage sensitivity upon changing turns
Current sensitivity is defined as deflection per unit current: \(S_i = \frac{\phi}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\). Since \(S_i \propto N\), doubling the turns (\(N \to 2N\)) directly doubles the current sensitivity. Voltage sensitivity is deflection per unit potential difference: \(S_v = \frac{\phi}{V} = \frac{\phi}{I R_G} = \frac{N A B}{k R_G}\), where \(R_G\) is the resistance of the galvanometer coil. When the number of turns doubles, the total length of the wire used for the coil doubles, which simultaneously doubles the coil resistance (\(R_G \to 2R_G\)). Therefore, \(S_v' = \frac{(2N) A B}{k (2R_G)} = \frac{N A B}{k R_G} = S_v\), leaving voltage sensitivity unchanged. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of voltmeter conversion methodology
A voltmeter is designed to measure the potential difference across two points in a circuit branch and must be connected in parallel with that branch. To avoid altering the existing current in the circuit, the voltmeter must have a very large internal resistance so that it draws minimal current. This is accomplished by connecting a large resistance \(R\) in series with the galvanometer coil of resistance \(R_G\), resulting in a high total resistance \(R_V = R_G + R\). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 4: Synthesis and conclusion
All three propositions regarding soft iron core utility, sensitivity scaling behavior, and voltmeter series-resistance conversion are scientifically verified and correct. Therefore, Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

चरण 1: धारामापी में नर्म लोहे के क्रोड के कार्य का विश्लेषण
चल कुंडली धारामापी में अवतल चुंबकीय ध्रुवों के साथ कुंडली के भीतर एक बेलनाकार नर्म लोहे का क्रोड रखा जाता है। नर्म लोहे की उच्च चुंबकशीलता चुंबकीय फ्लक्स रेखाओं को केंद्रित कर क्षेत्र की तीव्रता को बहुत बढ़ा देती है। इसके अतिरिक्त, बेलनाकार आकृति के कारण चुंबकीय क्षेत्र त्रिज्य हो जाता है, जिससे प्रत्येक कोणीय स्थिति में कुंडली का तल क्षेत्र रेखाओं के समांतर रहता है (\(\sin\theta = 1\)) और विक्षेपक बल-आघूर्ण सदैव \(\tau = N I A B\) बना रहता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: फेरों की संख्या बदलने पर धारा एवं वोल्टता सुग्राहिता का विश्लेषण
धारा सुग्राहिता प्रति एकांक धारा विक्षेप होती है: \(S_i = \frac{\phi}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\)। चूँकि \(S_i \propto N\), फेरों की संख्या \(N\) से \(2N\) करने पर धारा सुग्राहिता दोगुनी हो जाती है। वोल्टता सुग्राहिता \(S_v = \frac{\phi}{V} = \frac{N A B}{k R_G}\) होती है। फेरों की संख्या दोगुनी करने पर तार की कुल लंबाई भी दोगुनी हो जाती है, जिससे कुंडली का प्रतिरोध भी \(R_G\) से बढ़कर \(2R_G\) हो जाता है। अतः \(S_v' = \frac{(2N) A B}{k (2R_G)} = S_v\) अपरिवर्तित रहती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: वोल्टमीटर रूपांतरण विधि का विश्लेषण
वोल्टमीटर परिपथ के किन्हीं दो बिंदुओं के बीच विभवांतर मापने के लिए समांतर क्रम में जोड़ा जाता है। परिपथ की मूल धारा में न्यूनतम विक्षोभ हो, इसके लिए वोल्टमीटर का प्रतिरोध अत्यंत उच्च होना चाहिए। यह उद्देश्य धारामापी कुंडली के श्रेणीक्रम में एक उच्च मान का प्रतिरोध \(R\) जोड़कर प्राप्त किया जाता है, जिससे कुल प्रतिरोध \(R_V = R_G + R\) बहुत अधिक हो जाता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: संश्लेषण एवं निष्कर्ष
नर्म लोहे के क्रोड के प्रभाव, सुग्राहिता के परिवर्तन तथा वोल्टमीटर रूपांतरण से संबंधित तीनों कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं। अतः कथन I, कथन II और कथन III तीनों सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I, कथन II और कथन III तीनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct.
Statement I and Statement III only are correct.
Statement II and Statement III only are correct.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MATCH_MCQ_Q01 - SI units of electromagnetic quantities

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Physical Quantity) List II (SI Unit)
(A) Magnetic Field (\(B\)) (I) \(\text{A m}^2\)
(B) Magnetic Dipole Moment (\(m\)) (II) \(\text{T}\)
(C) Permeability of Free Space (\(\mu_0\)) (III) \(\text{N m rad}^{-1}\)
(D) Torsional Constant of Suspension Spring (\(k\)) (IV) \(\text{T m A}^{-1}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: SI Unit of Magnetic Field (\(B\))
The magnetic Lorentz force on a moving charge is given by \(F = q v B \sin\theta\). Solving for the magnetic field gives \(B = \frac{F}{q v \sin\theta}\). In SI units, this is \(\frac{\text{N}}{\text{C}\cdot\text{m s}^{-1}} = \frac{\text{N}}{\text{A}\cdot\text{m}}\), which is defined as the tesla (\(\text{T}\)). Therefore, Magnetic Field (\(B\)) corresponds to \(\text{T}\).

Step 2: SI Unit of Magnetic Dipole Moment (\(m\))
The magnetic dipole moment of a current-carrying planar coil of \(N\) turns and area \(A\) carrying current \(I\) is defined as \(m = N I A\). The SI unit of electric current is ampere (\(\text{A}\)) and that of area is square metre (\(\text{m}^2\)). Thus, the SI unit of magnetic dipole moment is \(\text{A m}^2\). Therefore, Magnetic Dipole Moment (\(m\)) corresponds to \(\text{A m}^2\).

Step 3: SI Unit of Permeability of Free Space (\(\mu_0\))
From Ampere's circuital law or the magnetic field around a straight conductor \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\), we obtain \(\mu_0 = \frac{2\pi r B}{I}\). Substituting the SI units gives \(\frac{\text{m}\cdot\text{T}}{\text{A}} = \text{T m A}^{-1}\) (equivalently \(\text{N A}^{-2}\)). Therefore, Permeability of Free Space (\(\mu_0\)) corresponds to \(\text{T m A}^{-1}\).

Step 4: SI Unit of Torsional Constant of Suspension Spring (\(k\))
In a moving coil galvanometer, the restoring torque exerted by the suspension spring or phosphor bronze strip is given by \(\tau = k \theta\), where \(\tau\) is the restoring torque and \(\theta\) is the angular deflection in radians. Thus, \(k = \frac{\tau}{\theta}\). The SI unit of torque is newton metre (\(\text{N m}\)) and that of angle is radian (\(\text{rad}\)), giving \(\text{N m rad}^{-1}\). Therefore, Torsional Constant (\(k\)) corresponds to \(\text{N m rad}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence between the physical quantities and their SI units is: Magnetic Field (\(B\)) pairs with (II), Magnetic Dipole Moment (\(m\)) pairs with (I), Permeability of Free Space (\(\mu_0\)) pairs with (IV), and Torsional Constant (\(k\)) pairs with (III). Hence, the correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MATCH_MCQ_Q02 - Magnetic field expressions for current configurations

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Current Distribution / Position) List II (Magnetic Field Magnitude)
(A) Centre of a flat circular loop of radius \(R\) carrying current \(I\) (I) \(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\)
(B) Distance \(r\) from a long straight wire carrying current \(I\) (II) \(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 R}\)
(C) Interior of a long ideal solenoid carrying current \(I\) with \(n\) turns per unit length (III) \(\dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2 x^3}\)
(D) Axis of a circular loop of radius \(R\) at large distance \(x \gg R\) (IV) \(\mu_0 n I\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Magnetic Field at the Centre of a Circular Loop
From the Biot-Savart law, the magnetic field at the centre of a flat single-turn circular loop of radius \(R\) carrying current \(I\) is obtained by integrating \(d B = \frac{\mu_0 I \, d l}{4\pi R^2}\) over the perimeter \(2\pi R\), yielding \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I (2\pi R)}{4\pi R^2} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 R}\). Therefore, the centre of a flat circular loop corresponds to \(\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 R}\).

Step 2: Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Current-Carrying Wire
Applying Ampere's circuital law along a concentric circular path of radius \(r\) perpendicular to a long straight wire carrying current \(I\), we have \(\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 I\). Solving for \(B\) gives \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\). Therefore, the distance \(r\) from a long straight wire corresponds to \(\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\).

Step 3: Magnetic Field Inside a Long Ideal Solenoid
Applying Ampere's circuital law to a rectangular loop enclosing \(n h\) turns of a long ideal solenoid carrying current \(I\), the field outside is negligible and along the axis it is uniform: \(B h = \mu_0 (n h I)\), which yields \(B = \mu_0 n I\). Therefore, the interior of a long ideal solenoid corresponds to \(\mu_0 n I\).

Step 4: Magnetic Field on the Axis of a Circular Loop at Large Distance
The axial magnetic field of a circular current loop of radius \(R\) at an axial distance \(x\) from the centre is given by \(B = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}\). For points far away along the axis such that \(x \gg R\), this expression simplifies to \(B \approx \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2 x^3}\). Therefore, the axis of a circular loop at large distance corresponds to \(\frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2 x^3}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence between current configurations and their magnetic fields is: The centre of a circular loop pairs with (II), the straight wire pairs with (I), the interior of a solenoid pairs with (IV), and the distant axial point of a loop pairs with (III). Hence, the correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MATCH_MCQ_Q03 - Charged particle motion in magnetic and electric fields

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Motion / Device Parameter) List II (Governing Mathematical Expression)
(A) Cyclotron angular frequency (\(\omega_c\)) (I) \(\dfrac{E}{B}\)
(B) Pitch of helical trajectory (\(p\)) (II) \(\dfrac{2\pi m v_\parallel}{q B}\)
(C) Condition for undeflected motion in crossed fields (\(v\)) (III) \(\dfrac{q B}{m}\)
(D) Radius of circular trajectory in uniform \(B\) (\(r\)) (IV) \(\dfrac{m v_\perp}{q B}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cyclotron Angular Frequency (\(\omega_c\))
When a charged particle of mass \(m\) and charge \(q\) moves in a circular path perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field \(B\), the magnetic Lorentz force provides the necessary centripetal force: \(\frac{m v^2}{r} = q v B\). Since the linear speed is related to angular frequency by \(v = \omega_c r\), substituting gives \(m \omega_c^2 r = q (\omega_c r) B\), which simplifies to \(\omega_c = \frac{q B}{m}\). Therefore, Cyclotron angular frequency corresponds to \(\frac{q B}{m}\).

Step 2: Pitch of Helical Trajectory (\(p\))
When the velocity vector of a charged particle makes an arbitrary angle with the uniform magnetic field, the velocity resolves into a parallel component \(v_\parallel\) and a perpendicular component \(v_\perp\). The period of circular revolution in the plane perpendicular to the field is \(T = \frac{2\pi r}{v_\perp} = \frac{2\pi m}{q B}\). The pitch \(p\) is the linear distance traversed along the magnetic field during one complete revolution: \(p = v_\parallel T = v_\parallel \left(\frac{2\pi m}{q B}\right) = \frac{2\pi m v_\parallel}{q B}\). Therefore, Pitch of helical trajectory corresponds to \(\frac{2\pi m v_\parallel}{q B}\).

Step 3: Condition for Undeflected Motion in Crossed Fields (\(v\))
In a velocity selector with mutually perpendicular electric field \(\vec{E}\) and magnetic field \(\vec{B}\), the electric force is \(\vec{F}_e = q \vec{E}\) and the magnetic force is \(\vec{F}_m = q (\vec{v} \times \vec{B})\). For the particle to pass undeflected, the net Lorentz force must be zero: \(\vec{F}_e + \vec{F}_m = 0\), which requires their magnitudes to balance: \(q E = q v B\), giving \(v = \frac{E}{B}\). Therefore, Condition for undeflected motion in crossed fields corresponds to \(\frac{E}{B}\).

Step 4: Radius of Circular Trajectory (\(r\))
The perpendicular velocity component \(v_\perp\) causes circular motion in the transverse plane where the magnetic force acts as centripetal force: \(\frac{m v_\perp^2}{r} = q v_\perp B\). Solving for the radius of orbit gives \(r = \frac{m v_\perp}{q B}\). Therefore, Radius of circular trajectory corresponds to \(\frac{m v_\perp}{q B}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence between the dynamical parameters and expressions is: Cyclotron angular frequency pairs with (III), Pitch of helical trajectory pairs with (II), Undeflected motion condition pairs with (I), and Radius of circular trajectory pairs with (IV). Hence, the correct combination is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_MATCH_MCQ_Q04 - Moving coil galvanometer parameters and circuit conversions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Galvanometer Parameter / Conversion) List II (Mathematical Expression)
(A) Current Sensitivity of Galvanometer (\(I_s\)) (I) \(\dfrac{N A B}{k R_g}\)
(B) Voltage Sensitivity of Galvanometer (\(V_s\)) (II) \(\dfrac{I_g R_g}{I - I_g}\)
(C) Shunt resistance (\(S\)) to convert into an ammeter of range \(I\) (III) \(\dfrac{N A B}{k}\)
(D) Series resistance (\(R\)) to convert into a voltmeter of range \(V\) (IV) \(\dfrac{V}{I_g} - R_g\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Current Sensitivity of Galvanometer (\(I_s\))
In a moving coil galvanometer with radial magnetic field, the deflecting magnetic torque is \(\tau = N I A B\) and the restoring torque is \(\tau = k \theta\). In equilibrium, \(k \theta = N I A B\), which gives the angular deflection per unit current as \(I_s = \frac{\theta}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\). Therefore, Current Sensitivity corresponds to \(\frac{N A B}{k}\).

Step 2: Voltage Sensitivity of Galvanometer (\(V_s\))
The voltage sensitivity is defined as the deflection produced per unit applied voltage: \(V_s = \frac{\theta}{V} = \frac{\theta}{I R_g}\), where \(R_g\) is the resistance of the galvanometer coil. Substituting \(\frac{\theta}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\) yields \(V_s = \frac{N A B}{k R_g}\). Therefore, Voltage Sensitivity corresponds to \(\frac{N A B}{k R_g}\).

Step 3: Shunt Resistance for Ammeter Conversion (\(S\))
To convert a galvanometer of internal resistance \(R_g\) and full-scale deflection current \(I_g\) into an ammeter measuring up to total current \(I\), a low shunt resistance \(S\) is connected in parallel with the coil. Since both branches share the same potential difference, \(I_g R_g = (I - I_g) S\). Solving for the shunt resistance gives \(S = \frac{I_g R_g}{I - I_g}\). Therefore, Shunt resistance corresponds to \(\frac{I_g R_g}{I - I_g}\).

Step 4: Series Resistance for Voltmeter Conversion (\(R\))
To convert the galvanometer into a voltmeter capable of reading a potential difference up to \(V\), a large resistance \(R\) is connected in series with the coil. The total potential difference across the combination when full-scale current \(I_g\) flows is \(V = I_g (R_g + R)\). Solving for the series resistance gives \(R_g + R = \frac{V}{I_g}\), hence \(R = \frac{V}{I_g} - R_g\). Therefore, Series resistance corresponds to \(\frac{V}{I_g} - R_g\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence between the galvanometer metrics and their expressions is: Current Sensitivity pairs with (III), Voltage Sensitivity pairs with (I), Shunt resistance pairs with (II), and Series resistance pairs with (IV). Hence, the correct combination is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Force on a charge moving perpendicular to a magnetic field

questiontext.text: A proton carrying a charge of \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\) enters a uniform magnetic field of \(0.25\text{ T}\) with a speed of \(4.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\) at right angles to the direction of the field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the proton?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Charge of the proton, \(q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).
Magnetic field strength, \(B = 0.25\text{ T}\).
Velocity of the proton, \(v = 4.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\).
Angle between velocity vector and magnetic field vector, \(\theta = 90^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The magnetic field is uniform and static. Relativistic effects are neglected since \(v \ll c\). The force magnitude is scalar.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic Lorentz force on a moving charge is given by:
\[F = q v B \sin\theta\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the formula:
\[F = (1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (4.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}) \times (0.25\text{ T}) \times \sin(90^\circ)\]
Since \(\sin(90^\circ) = 1\):
\[F = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1.0 \times 10^{6} = 1.6 \times 10^{-13}\text{ N}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units \(\text{C} \cdot \text{m s}^{-1} \cdot \text{T} = \text{N}\) are consistent.
Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the proton is \(1.6 \times 10^{-13}\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Magnetic field at the center of a circular coil

questiontext.text: A circular coil of wire consisting of \(50\) turns, each of radius \(8.0\text{ cm}\), carries a current of \(0.40\text{ A}\). What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of turns in the circular coil, \(N = 50\).
Radius of the coil, \(R = 8.0\text{ cm} = 0.08\text{ m}\).
Current carried by the coil, \(I = 0.40\text{ A}\).
Permeability of free space, \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The coil is closely wound such that all turns can be considered to have the same radius \(R\) and lie in the same plane.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic field at the centre of a flat circular coil of \(N\) turns is given by Biot-Savart law as:
\[B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2R}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values:
\[B = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}) \times 50 \times 0.40\text{ A}}{2 \times 0.08\text{ m}}\]
Simplify the numerator and denominator:
\[B = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 20}{0.16} = \frac{80\pi \times 10^{-7}}{0.16} = 500\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\]
Using \(\pi \approx 3.1416\):
\[B = 500 \times 3.1416 \times 10^{-7} = 1.5708 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T} \approx 1.57 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional analysis yields tesla (\(\text{T}\)), and the numerical magnitude is physically sound.
Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is \(1.57 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Magnetic field inside a long solenoid

questiontext.text: A closely wound solenoid of length \(0.5\text{ m}\) has \(500\) turns of wire. If it carries a current of \(2.0\text{ A}\), what is the magnetic field inside the solenoid near its centre?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of the solenoid, \(L = 0.5\text{ m}\).
Total number of turns, \(N = 500\).
Current, \(I = 2.0\text{ A}\).
Permeability constant, \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The solenoid is considered sufficiently long so that end effects can be neglected near the centre.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic field inside an ideal long solenoid near its centre is given by Ampere's circuital law as:
\[B = \mu_0 n I\]
where \(n = \frac{N}{L}\) is the number of turns per unit length.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the turn density \(n\):
\[n = \frac{500}{0.5\text{ m}} = 1000\text{ turns m}^{-1}\]
Substitute \(n\) and \(I\) into the field equation:
\[B = (4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}) \times (1000\text{ m}^{-1}) \times (2.0\text{ A})\]
\[B = 8\pi \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}\]
With \(\pi \approx 3.1416\):
\[B = 8 \times 3.1416 \times 10^{-4} = 2.513 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T} \approx 2.51 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The unit is tesla and the order of magnitude corresponds to typical laboratory solenoids.
Therefore, the magnetic field inside the solenoid near its centre is \(2.51 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Magnetic dipole moment of a flat circular loop

questiontext.text: A circular coil of \(20\) turns and radius \(10\text{ cm}\) carries a steady current of \(3.0\text{ A}\). What is the magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment associated with the coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of turns, \(N = 20\).
Radius of the coil, \(R = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\).
Current, \(I = 3.0\text{ A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The coil is planar. The magnetic moment vector points perpendicular to the plane of the coil according to the right-hand grip rule.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment \(m\) of a current-carrying planar coil is given by:
\[m = N I A\]
where \(A = \pi R^2\) is the cross-sectional area enclosed by each turn.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the area \(A\):
\[A = \pi R^2 = \pi (0.10\text{ m})^2 = 0.01\pi\text{ m}^2\]
Compute the magnetic dipole moment:
\[m = 20 \times (3.0\text{ A}) \times (0.01\pi\text{ m}^2) = 0.60\pi\text{ A m}^2\]
Using \(\pi \approx 3.1416\):
\[m = 0.60 \times 3.1416 = 1.88496\text{ A m}^2 \approx 1.88\text{ A m}^2\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are \(\text{A} \cdot \text{m}^2\), which matches the SI unit of magnetic moment.
Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment associated with the coil is \(1.88\text{ A m}^{2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Force on a straight current carrying conductor in magnetic field

questiontext.text: A straight wire of length \(1.5\text{ m}\) carries a current of \(2.0\text{ A}\) in a direction making an angle of \(30^\circ\) with a uniform magnetic field of \(0.40\text{ T}\). What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of the conductor, \(l = 1.5\text{ m}\).
Current in the conductor, \(I = 2.0\text{ A}\).
Angle with the magnetic field, \(\theta = 30^\circ\).
Magnetic field strength, \(B = 0.40\text{ T}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The conductor is straight and placed entirely within a uniform magnetic field.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire is given by:
\[F = I l B \sin\theta\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the formula:
\[F = (2.0\text{ A}) \times (1.5\text{ m}) \times (0.40\text{ T}) \times \sin(30^\circ)\]
Since \(\sin(30^\circ) = 0.5\):
\[F = 3.0 \times 0.40 \times 0.5 = 0.60\text{ N}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The product yields newtons correctly. At \(\theta = 30^\circ\), the force is half the maximum force \(1.20\text{ N}\).
Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic force on the wire is \(0.60\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Magnetic field at a distance from a long straight wire

questiontext.text: A long, straight horizontal wire carries a current of \(35\text{ A}\). What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a perpendicular distance of \(20\text{ cm}\) from the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Current carried by the straight wire, \(I = 35\text{ A}\).
Perpendicular distance from the wire, \(r = 20\text{ cm} = 0.20\text{ m}\).
Permeability constant, \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The wire is straight, infinitely long compared to \(r\), and surrounded by vacuum or air.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From Ampere's circuital law, the magnetic field at distance \(r\) from a long straight current-carrying wire is:
\[B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[B = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}) \times 35\text{ A}}{2\pi \times 0.20\text{ m}}\]
Simplify the factor \(\frac{4\pi}{2\pi} = 2\):
\[B = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 35}{0.20} = \frac{70 \times 10^{-7}}{0.20} = 350 \times 10^{-7}\text{ T} = 3.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are in tesla and \(35\,\mu\text{T}\) is physically typical for this current and distance.
Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic field at the given distance is \(3.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Force per unit length between two parallel current carrying wires

questiontext.text: Two long, straight parallel wires separated by a distance of \(10\text{ cm}\) in air carry currents of \(4.0\text{ A}\) and \(5.0\text{ A}\) in the same direction. What is the magnitude of the force per unit length exerted by one wire on the other?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Current in the first wire, \(I_1 = 4.0\text{ A}\).
Current in the second wire, \(I_2 = 5.0\text{ A}\).
Separation distance between the wires, \(d = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\).
Permeability constant, \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The wires are infinitely long, parallel, and placed in vacuum/air. Parallel currents in the same direction attract each other.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of the magnetic force per unit length \(f\) between two parallel current-carrying wires is:
\[f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values:
\[f = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 4.0 \times 5.0}{2\pi \times 0.10}\]
Cancel \(2\pi\) into \(4\pi\) to get \(2\):
\[f = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 20.0}{0.10} = \frac{40.0 \times 10^{-7}}{0.10} = 400 \times 10^{-7}\text{ N m}^{-1} = 4.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ N m}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The resulting unit \(\text{N m}^{-1}\) is correct for force per unit length.
Therefore, the magnitude of the force per unit length exerted by one wire on the other is \(4.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ N m}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Radius of circular path of electron in uniform magnetic field

questiontext.text: An electron of mass \(9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\) and charge magnitude \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\) is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of \(500\text{ V}\) and then enters perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field of \(0.20\text{ T}\). What is the radius of the circular path traced by the electron?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of electron, \(m = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\).
Charge of electron, \(q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).
Accelerating potential difference, \(V = 500\text{ V}\).
Magnetic field strength, \(B = 0.20\text{ T}\).
Entrance angle, \(\theta = 90^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Kinetic energy gained by the electron is \(K = qV\). The speed is non-relativistic.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The radius \(r\) of circular motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field is:
\[r = \frac{m v}{q B} = \frac{p}{q B}\]
Since \(K = \frac{p^2}{2m} = qV\), the momentum is \(p = \sqrt{2mqV}\).
Thus:
\[r = \frac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB} = \frac{1}{B}\sqrt{\frac{2mV}{q}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate momentum \(p\):
\[p = \sqrt{2 \times (9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (500\text{ V})}\]
\[p = \sqrt{2 \times 9.1 \times 1.6 \times 500 \times 10^{-50}} = \sqrt{14560 \times 10^{-50}} = \sqrt{1.456 \times 10^{-46}} \approx 1.2066 \times 10^{-23}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\]
Now compute the radius \(r\):
\[r = \frac{p}{qB} = \frac{1.2066 \times 10^{-23}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}}{(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (0.20\text{ T})}\]
\[r = \frac{1.2066 \times 10^{-23}}{3.2 \times 10^{-20}} = 0.37707 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 3.77 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The resulting unit is metres and the value is sub-millimetre, as expected for high magnetic field and light electrons.
Therefore, the radius of the circular path traced by the electron is \(3.77 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Pitch of helical path of a charged particle in magnetic field

questiontext.text: A proton of mass \(1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\) and charge \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\) enters a uniform magnetic field of \(0.50\text{ T}\) with a speed of \(2.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\) at an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the magnetic field lines. What is the pitch of the helical path traced by the proton?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of proton, \(m = 1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\).
Charge of proton, \(q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).
Speed of proton, \(v = 2.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\).
Magnetic field strength, \(B = 0.50\text{ T}\).
Angle with field, \(\theta = 60^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The velocity resolves into two components: parallel to the field \(v_\parallel = v\cos\theta\), and perpendicular to the field \(v_\perp = v\sin\theta\). The parallel component remains unchanged while the perpendicular component undergoes uniform circular motion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The time period of one revolution in the circular plane is:
\[T = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}\]
The pitch \(p\) of the helix is the linear distance advanced along the field in one time period:
\[p = v_\parallel T = (v\cos\theta) \left(\frac{2\pi m}{qB}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the time period \(T\):
\[T = \frac{2\pi \times (1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg})}{(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (0.50\text{ T})} = \frac{3.34\pi \times 10^{-27}}{0.80 \times 10^{-19}} = 4.175\pi \times 10^{-8}\text{ s} \approx 1.3116 \times 10^{-7}\text{ s}\]
Calculate the parallel velocity component:
\[v_\parallel = v\cos(60^\circ) = (2.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}) \times 0.5 = 1.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\]
Calculate the pitch \(p\):
\[p = v_\parallel T = (1.0 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}) \times (1.3116 \times 10^{-7}\text{ s}) = 0.13116\text{ m} \approx 1.31 \times 10^{-1}\text{ m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The pitch is in metres and has positive physical length.
Therefore, the pitch of the helical path traced by the proton is \(1.31 \times 10^{-1}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Shunt resistance to convert galvanometer into ammeter

questiontext.text: A galvanometer has a resistance of \(12\text{ }\Omega\) and the meter shows full scale deflection for a current of \(3.0\text{ mA}\). How should it be modified to convert it into an ammeter of range \(0\) to \(6.0\text{ A}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Galvanometer resistance, \(G = 12\text{ }\Omega\).
Current for full scale deflection, \(I_g = 3.0\text{ mA} = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}\).
Required maximum current range, \(I = 6.0\text{ A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
To measure a larger current without burning the coil, a low resistance (shunt) \(S\) must be connected in parallel with the galvanometer coil.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Since the galvanometer and shunt are connected in parallel, potential difference across both is identical:
\[I_g G = (I - I_g) S \implies S = \frac{I_g G}{I - I_g}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the formula:
\[I - I_g = 6.0\text{ A} - 0.003\text{ A} = 5.997\text{ A}\]
Compute the required shunt resistance \(S\):
\[S = \frac{(3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}) \times 12\text{ }\Omega}{5.997\text{ A}} = \frac{0.036}{5.997}\text{ }\Omega \approx 0.006003\text{ }\Omega = 6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ }\Omega\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The shunt resistance is much smaller than the galvanometer coil resistance, allowing practically all the current to bypass the galvanometer.
Therefore, the required modification is a shunt resistance of \(6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ }\Omega\text{ in parallel}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Series resistance to convert galvanometer into voltmeter

questiontext.text: A galvanometer of resistance \(25\text{ }\Omega\) gives full scale deflection with a current of \(2.0\text{ mA}\). What value of series resistance is required to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to \(10\text{ V}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Galvanometer resistance, \(G = 25\text{ }\Omega\).
Full scale deflection current, \(I_g = 2.0\text{ mA} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}\).
Desired voltage range, \(V = 10\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
To measure a high voltage, a large resistance \(R\) is connected in series with the galvanometer so that the total voltage drops across the series combination when current \(I_g\) passes.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From Ohm's law applied to the series combination:
\[V = I_g (G + R) \implies R = \frac{V}{I_g} - G\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the total resistance required:
\[R_{\text{total}} = \frac{V}{I_g} = \frac{10\text{ V}}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}} = 5000\text{ }\Omega\]
Subtract the internal resistance of the galvanometer:
\[R = 5000\text{ }\Omega - 25\text{ }\Omega = 4975\text{ }\Omega\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The required series resistance is positive and significantly larger than \(G\).
Therefore, the value of series resistance required is \(4975\text{ }\Omega\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Change in current and voltage sensitivity with coil parameters

questiontext.text: A moving coil galvanometer has \(N\) turns and resistance \(R\). If the number of turns is doubled to \(2N\) using wire of the same material and cross-sectional area (so the resistance also doubles to \(2R\)), by what factor does its voltage sensitivity change?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial number of turns \(= N\), initial resistance \(= R\).
Final number of turns \(= N' = 2N\), final resistance \(= R' = 2R\).
Magnetic field \(B\), coil area \(A\), and restoring torsion constant \(k\) remain constant.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Current sensitivity is defined as deflection per unit current, \(S_i = \frac{\phi}{I}\).
Voltage sensitivity is defined as deflection per unit voltage, \(S_v = \frac{\phi}{V}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
At equilibrium, deflecting torque equals restoring torque:
\[N I A B = k \phi \implies \frac{\phi}{I} = \frac{N A B}{k}\]
Using \(V = I R\):
\[S_v = \frac{\phi}{V} = \frac{\phi}{I R} = \frac{N A B}{k R}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the new parameters into the expression for voltage sensitivity \(S_v'\):
\[S_v' = \frac{N' A B}{k R'} = \frac{(2N) A B}{k (2R)} = \frac{2}{2} \left(\frac{N A B}{k R}\right) = S_v\]
The factor of \(2\) in the numerator cancels the factor of \(2\) in the denominator.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
While current sensitivity doubles when turns double, voltage sensitivity is independent of this change because coil resistance increases proportionally.
Therefore, the voltage sensitivity remains unchanged.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Magnetic field at center of a circular arc

questiontext.text: A wire carrying a current of \(10\text{ A}\) is bent into a circular arc of radius \(5.0\text{ cm}\) subtending an angle of \(120^\circ\) at its centre. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field produced at the centre of curvature?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Current in the wire, \(I = 10\text{ A}\).
Radius of the circular arc, \(R = 5.0\text{ cm} = 0.05\text{ m}\).
Subtended angle, \(\theta = 120^\circ = \frac{120\pi}{180} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ rad}\).
Permeability constant, \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The contributions from current-carrying leads connecting to the arc are neglected or directed radially so their cross product \(d\mathbf{l} \times \hat{\mathbf{r}} = 0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic field at the centre of a full circular loop of radius \(R\) is \(B_{\text{full}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\).
For an arc subtending an angle \(\theta\) (in radians), the field is proportional to the fraction of the complete circle:
\[B = \left(\frac{\theta}{2\pi}\right) \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R} = \frac{\mu_0 I \theta}{4\pi R}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values with \(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\):
\[B = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}) \times 10\text{ A} \times (2\pi / 3)}{4\pi \times 0.05\text{ m}}\]
Cancel \(4\pi\) in numerator and denominator:
\[B = \frac{10^{-7} \times 10 \times \frac{2\pi}{3}}{0.05} = \frac{10^{-6} \times \frac{2\pi}{3}}{0.05} = \frac{2\pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.15} = \frac{40\pi}{3} \times 10^{-6}\text{ T}\]
Using \(\pi \approx 3.1416\):
\[B = \frac{40 \times 3.1416}{3} \times 10^{-6} = \frac{125.664}{3} \times 10^{-6} \approx 41.89 \times 10^{-6}\text{ T} = 4.19 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(120^\circ\) is one-third of \(360^\circ\), the field is exactly one-third of the field of a complete loop: \(\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10}{2 \times 0.05} = \frac{1}{3} \times 1.257 \times 10^{-4} = 4.19 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}\).
Therefore, the magnitude of the magnetic field produced at the centre of curvature is \(4.19 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Ratio of magnetic field at center to axial point of circular loop

questiontext.text: A circular loop of radius \(R\) carries a steady current \(I\). At what distance along the axis of the loop from its centre is the magnetic field equal to \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of circular loop \(= R\).
Current carried by loop \(= I\).
Condition: \(B_{\text{axis}}(x) = \frac{1}{8} B_{\text{centre}}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The loop is circular and planar, and the point is located along the principal axis perpendicular to the plane of the loop passing through its centre.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is:
\[B_{\text{centre}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\]
The magnetic field at an axial point distance \(x\) from the centre is:
\[B_{\text{axis}}(x) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(x^2 + R^2)^{3/2}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Form the ratio of the two fields:
\[\frac{B_{\text{axis}}}{B_{\text{centre}}} = \frac{R^3}{(x^2 + R^2)^{3/2}} = \left(\frac{R^2}{x^2 + R^2}\right)^{3/2}\]
Equating this ratio to \(\frac{1}{8}\):
\[\left(\frac{R^2}{x^2 + R^2}\right)^{3/2} = \frac{1}{8} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3\]
Taking the cube root on both sides:
\[\left(\frac{R^2}{x^2 + R^2}\right)^{1/2} = \frac{1}{2}\]
Squaring both sides:
\[\frac{R^2}{x^2 + R^2} = \frac{1}{4} \implies x^2 + R^2 = 4R^2 \implies x^2 = 3R^2 \implies x = \sqrt{3}\,R\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Substituting \(x = \sqrt{3}\,R\) into the axial formula gives \((x^2 + R^2)^{3/2} = (4R^2)^{3/2} = 8R^3\), which reproduces the factor of \(\frac{1}{8}\).
Therefore, the distance along the axis from the centre of the loop is \(\sqrt{3}\,R\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Torque on a rectangular coil in a uniform magnetic field

questiontext.text: A rectangular coil of dimensions \(10\text{ cm} \times 5.0\text{ cm}\) consists of \(100\) turns and carries a current of \(1.2\text{ A}\). It is suspended in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of \(0.20\text{ T}\) such that the normal to the plane of the coil makes an angle of \(30^\circ\) with the magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the torque acting on the coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Dimensions of the coil: length \(a = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\), width \(b = 5.0\text{ cm} = 0.05\text{ m}\).
Number of turns, \(N = 100\).
Current, \(I = 1.2\text{ A}\).
Magnetic field strength, \(B = 0.20\text{ T}\).
Angle between the normal to the coil and the field, \(\theta = 30^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The coil is rigid and the magnetic field is uniform across the entire area of the coil.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The torque \(\tau\) on a current-carrying planar coil is given by:
\[\tau = N I A B \sin\theta\]
where \(A = a \times b\) is the area of the rectangular loop.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the area of the coil:
\[A = 0.10\text{ m} \times 0.05\text{ m} = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2\]
Calculate the magnetic dipole moment \(m\):
\[m = N I A = 100 \times 1.2\text{ A} \times 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2 = 0.60\text{ A m}^2\]
Calculate the torque:
\[\tau = m B \sin(30^\circ) = (0.60\text{ A m}^2) \times (0.20\text{ T}) \times 0.5 = 0.060\text{ N m} = 6.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ N m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are \(\text{N m}\), which is consistent with torque.
Therefore, the magnitude of the torque acting on the coil is \(6.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ N m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Orbital magnetic moment of hydrogen electron

questiontext.text: In a hydrogen atom, an electron of charge \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\) revolves around the nucleus in an orbit of radius \(5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\) with an orbital speed of \(2.2 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\). What is the orbital magnetic dipole moment of the electron?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Charge of electron, \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).
Radius of orbit, \(r = 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\).
Speed of revolution, \(v = 2.2 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The revolving electron constitutes an effective closed circular current loop.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The effective current is \(I = \frac{e}{T} = \frac{e v}{2\pi r}\).
The area of the circular orbit is \(A = \pi r^2\).
The magnetic moment is given by:
\[\mu_l = I A = \left(\frac{e v}{2\pi r}\right) (\pi r^2) = \frac{1}{2} e v r\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the expression:
\[\mu_l = \frac{1}{2} \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (2.2 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}) \times (5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m})\]
\[\mu_l = 0.5 \times 1.6 \times 2.2 \times 5.3 \times 10^{-19 + 6 - 11}\]
\[\mu_l = 0.8 \times 2.2 \times 5.3 \times 10^{-24} = 1.76 \times 5.3 \times 10^{-24} = 9.328 \times 10^{-24}\text{ A m}^2 \approx 9.33 \times 10^{-24}\text{ A m}^2\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
This value is extremely close to the standard Bohr magneton \(\mu_B = 9.27 \times 10^{-24}\text{ A m}^2\), which confirms physical validity.
Therefore, the orbital magnetic dipole moment of the electron is \(9.33 \times 10^{-24}\text{ A m}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Velocity selector electric and magnetic field balance

questiontext.text: A velocity selector consists of mutually perpendicular uniform electric and magnetic fields. If the electric field has a magnitude of \(6.0 \times 10^{4}\text{ V m}^{-1}\) and the magnetic field has a magnitude of \(0.15\text{ T}\), what speed must an ion have in order to pass through the selector undeflected?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Electric field magnitude, \(E = 6.0 \times 10^{4}\text{ V m}^{-1}\).
Magnetic field magnitude, \(B = 0.15\text{ T}\).
The electric and magnetic fields and the particle velocity are mutually perpendicular.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The net Lorentz force on the charged particle is zero, meaning the electric force and magnetic force balance each other exactly in magnitude and oppose each other in direction.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The Lorentz force equation is \(\mathbf{F} = q(\mathbf{E} + \mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B})\).
For undeflected motion:
\[qE = qvB \implies v = \frac{E}{B}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[v = \frac{6.0 \times 10^{4}\text{ V m}^{-1}}{0.15\text{ T}} = \frac{6.0 \times 10^{4}}{1.5 \times 10^{-1}} = 4.0 \times 10^{5}\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are \(\frac{\text{V m}^{-1}}{\text{T}} = \frac{\text{N C}^{-1}}{\text{N s C}^{-1}\text{ m}^{-1}} = \text{m s}^{-1}\), matching velocity.
Therefore, the speed required for the ion to pass undeflected is \(4.0 \times 10^{5}\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MOVING_CHARGES_AND_MAGNETISM_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Cyclotron resonance frequency of a proton

questiontext.text: A cyclotron's oscillator frequency is to be set to accelerate protons (mass \(m = 1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\), charge \(q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\)). If the operating magnetic field in the dees has a magnitude of \(0.66\text{ T}\), what is the required cyclotron frequency?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of proton, \(m = 1.67 imes 10^{-27} ext{ kg}\).
Charge of proton, \(q = 1.60 imes 10^{-19} ext{ C}\).
Magnetic field strength, \(B = 0.66 ext{ T}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The proton moves non-relativistically within the dees. In cyclotron resonance, the radiofrequency oscillator frequency matches the orbital frequency of the charged particle.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The cyclotron frequency (revolution frequency) is independent of velocity and radius, given by:
